reading.body:
CDW is a reseller of AI-ready hardware and services, not a builder of AI models or infrastructure.

The record shows a company whose AI position is entirely downstream of other firms' silicon. Its site names Surface Copilot+ PCs, a Logitech Rally AI Camera, and a Mac mini with an M6 chip, all sold as products for on-device workflows. The company's own framing is advisor and deployment partner. That places CDW in the distribution layer of AI, moving boxes and configuring them, rather than in the layer that decides how much compute gets built or where.

The filings show a regular reporting cadence through 2026, including two 10-Qs and a cluster of 8-Ks, with the most recent dated September 2026. That is the profile of an established public distributor. Nothing in the data ties CDW to data centers, power procurement, or grid constraints, and the industry classification is retail catalog and mail order. A reader looking for the compute buildout will not find it here.

What the data does not cover is scale. There are no revenue figures, no segment breakdowns, no customer counts, and no tracked products. The profile text is drawn from the company's own website, so it describes positioning rather than verified capability. The absence of lawsuits and MCP servers is a statement about what was tracked, not about what exists.

profile_text.body:
CDW is a public company founded in 1984 and headquartered in Vernon Hills, trading under the ticker CDW. It is registered with the SEC under CIK 0001402057. Its website describes it as a provider of information technology products, expertise and services for business, including hardware, software, fast shipping, large in-stock inventories and custom configurations.

The site's AI material is largely framed around readiness and deployment rather than products of its own. CDW describes helping organizations enforce data quality and governance as a foundation for trusted artificial intelligence, and presents infrastructure modernization as a path to AI readiness. It also describes tailored services for agencies moving legacy data centers toward artificial intelligence initiatives, and a people-first approach to AI in retail. Hardware it highlights includes Surface Laptops, Microsoft Surface Copilot+ PCs, the Logitech Rally AI Camera and Rally AI Camera Pro, and Mac mini with the M6 chip, all presented alongside CDW expertise to deploy, manage and scale.

The held record lists no products, no lawsuits and no MCP servers for CDW.
